What is a ball and socket joint? Where is it found?
questions.a: The round end of one bone fits in a cup of another, allowing movement in all directions - shoulder and hip.

questions.q: Which movements does the shoulder joint allow?
questions.a: Rotation, lifting, swinging the arm in circles - almost all directions.

questions.q: Why does the hip joint move less freely than the shoulder?
questions.a: Deeper socket and stronger ligaments trade some motion for body support.

questions.q: What is a hinge joint? Where does it occur?
questions.a: A joint moving in one direction like a door hinge - elbow and knee.

questions.q: Which directions can the elbow move?
questions.a: Only back and forth - it cannot rotate like the shoulder.

questions.q: Why is the knee called a hinge joint?
questions.a: It bends and straightens in one plane, like a door.

questions.q: What are fixed joints?
questions.a: Joints that allow no movement - the skull bones are joined like this.

questions.q: Where are fixed joints found in the body?
questions.a: In the skull, where plates are locked together protecting the brain.

questions.q: Why is a fixed skull useful?
questions.a: A rigid skull shields the delicate brain from blows.

questions.q: What is cartilage?
questions.a: A smooth, flexible tissue covering bone ends at joints, and shaping ear and nose.

questions.q: Why is cartilage important at joints?
questions.a: It reduces friction and absorbs shock so bones glide smoothly.

questions.q: Can you bend your ear bones? What makes ears bendable?
questions.a: Cartilage, not bone, gives the ear its flexible shape.

questions.q: How many legs and wings does a cockroach have?
questions.a: Three pairs of legs and two pairs of wings.

questions.q: Which muscles move a cockroach's legs?
questions.a: Muscles in the legs and thorax work in pairs to run fast.

questions.q: How do cockroach wings help it?
questions.a: It flies short distances to escape danger.

questions.q: How are birds' bones suited to flying?
questions.a: Their bones are hollow and light, reducing weight for flight.

questions.q: Which muscles power a bird's wings?
questions.a: Strong breast (flight) muscles attached to a boat-shaped breastbone.

questions.q: Name three bird features that help flight.
questions.a: Hollow bones, streamlined body, strong breast muscles and wing feathers.

questions.q: What is a streamlined body?
questions.a: A shape narrow at both ends that lets water or air flow past easily - as in fish and boats.

questions.q: How does a fish swim forward?
questions.a: It bends its body and tail side to side in curves, pushing water back and itself forward.

questions.q: What role do fins play in swimming?
questions.a: Fins steer, balance and stop the fish.

questions.q: How does a snake move without legs?
questions.a: It throws its body into looping curves, pushing against the ground to glide forward.

questions.q: What is a snake's slithering helped by?
questions.a: Broad belly scales that grip the ground as the body curves.

questions.q: Why can a snake move fast despite no limbs?
questions.a: Many muscles press against ground points in rhythm, driving it ahead quickly.
